title: The engine tests a model for new entities when every entity appears in every period
request: The owner chose the engine split for new entities: the planner's entity split was asked, never applied, because the engine refused time and entity together when every store reports every week.
spec: Forward in time and no entity on both sides, as the declared split means; the old way first; a simulation only when it cannot; seeded; the person told what it costs; the feasibility check is the split itself.
plan: time_group_split: the natural way, then held-out entities
folds that repeat it inside training
update the tests that asserted the old refusal
review, fix, rerun the practice set

decisions.decision: Hold out a quarter of the entities and score their rows after the 0.75 time cut
decisions.why: what a store opened next year faces: never trained on, and later in time

decisions.decision: Rows of held-out entities before the cut and of the others after it are used by neither
decisions.why: either would put the entity or the future on the training side
an interval over two held-out entities means little (the review)

decisions.decision: Five tests that asserted the refusal were changed, keeping their intent with data that still cannot be split
decisions.why: the refusal they guarded is now a split for most tables; the guard still holds where it cannot

change: dclab_rnd/expansion/datasets.py (time_group_split, _held_out_entities, _held_out_folds, time_group_feasible with the outcome and details, bundle extras), dclab_rnd/studio/engine.py (rows a day before the cut), dclab_rnd/tasks/path.py (the outcome in group_fits, the note), dclab_rnd/studio/team.py and agent_eval/journeys (the outcome in the check); tests.

findings.defect: The engine refused time and entity together when every entity recurs.
findings.scenario: Practice pr09, pr12: the planner's entity split could only be asked.
findings.cause: the latest rows held no unseen entity
findings.fix: seeded held-out entities after a time cut

findings.defect: The check said yes, the build refused a rare-class classification.
findings.scenario: 33 entities, positives in 3: feasible True, split ValueError (226 of 300 rare-class tables).
findings.cause: the check ran without the outcome
findings.fix: the outcome and task passed by every caller; rows without an outcome dropped; the error names the class reason

findings.defect: A day's rows were counted from training only, so the review share was a third too large.
findings.scenario: 40 stores a day, training sees 30: a capacity of 6 a day reviewed 20% instead of 15%.
findings.cause: training holds only the kept entities
findings.fix: count every row before the cut (bundle extras)

findings.scenario: assertGreaterEqual across the cut; no fold-order test; no rare-class test; no team test of the new default.
findings.fix: assertGreater; fold order; rare class; a team test with 120 recurring customers

findings.scenario: team and journeys: '0 of the last N rows are of one unseen before' when 25 existed.

findings.defect: The interval could rest on two entities.
findings.scenario: 8 entities: 50 test rows from 2 entities, a cluster bootstrap over 2 groups.

findings.defect: A refusal became a silent simulation.
findings.scenario: 40 stores x 52 weeks: 37.5% of rows used by neither, said only in the holdout description.
findings.fix: the plan's applied change carries a note with the unused share, said in the build message

measurements.name: Practice set v1 after the engine split
measurements.result: enforced 24 to 28 of 48; entity 0 to 4 applied (pr09, pr12 both seeds); builds failed 0; pr12 460 of 1,200 rows unused

outcome: Time and entity together now split for most tables: a quarter of the entities held out as new after a time cut, the cost said to the person. Too few entities or a class the split cannot hold is still refused, and the check says so before the build.
lessons: A feasibility check must be the code it predicts, called with the same inputs.
When a split throws data away, say how much.
risks: NumPy may change seeded draws across versions; the split fingerprint would then change.
The served model never sees the latest quarter of time.
The hyperparameter search skips these projects (its selection fold empties).
Home's page still describes time and group as the latest period with no entity on both sides.
